text: {"score":2,"justification":"The core numbers match the card (24.4%, 1.9%, 12.16, z 3.78, 78%, 30 docs, 0/14, 7 of 26). The summary has problems in its narrative and conclusions. It says 'Records complete after a follow-up about missing signatures', which has no basis in the packet. It says 'a sign notes may be inflated to match the bill', which is speculative and unsupported: 14 documented 99215s all supported high MDM, and only 2 of 30 documented claims were below billed. The 'inconclusive' leaning conflicts with the strong statistical evidence (13x expected, z 3.78) and with the 'weak evidence either way' framing. The 23% in the headline is 7/30, not the 7/26 stated in the rationale, so the denominator is mismatched and the headline mischaracterizes the finding. Next steps are generic: they do not name specific claims to request, and they ignore that documentation for the cited low-complexity 99215s (e.g., C0034539, C0034546) was not obtained. The cited examples C0034671 and C0034749 are below-billed 99214s, which do not support the high-99215 concern, and the two 99215 examples are fine but few. It also fails to note that 99215 documentation supported the billing, which is the key mitigating fact.","problems":["Headline '23%' is 7/30 but the body gives 7 of 26 (27%); inconsistent denominator, flagged by number check","'Records complete after a follow-up about missing signatures' is unsupported by the packet","'Sign notes may be inflated to match the bill' is speculative and not supported by the evidence (all documented 99215s supported high MDM)","Leaning 'inconclusive' and 'weak evidence either way' understates the strong statistical outlier signal and is internally inconsistent","Next steps are generic; they do not request documentation for the cited low-complexity 99215 claims","Cited below-billed 99214 examples do not bear on the 99215 upcoding concern; the summary doesn't note that the documented 99215s were supported"]}
